summary: Relax skill_match_batch_runs.input_file_id to NULLABLE (setup-flow S6, cinatra#2391: provider-neutral skill auto-matching) — ALTER TABLE skill_match_batch_runs ALTER COLUMN input_file_id DROP NOT NULL. The column was NOT NULL because every run was an OpenAI v1 batch whose submit response carried a provider input-file id; the provider-neutral pipeline records runs that legitimately have none (neutral batch-v2 submissions expose no provider file ids, and synchronous fan-out runs on batch-less providers — 'sync-' batch ids — never touch a provider file). Classified destructive as a rewrite of a deployed column's definition; the operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap shape in src/lib/drizzle-store.ts + src/lib/skill-lifecycle-schema.ts, shipped in the SAME PR so fresh installs bootstrap the nullable shape and ledger-fake the chain while existing deployments execute this module at boot / cinatra db migrate. No row is touched: every existing row carries a non-null value (the old pipeline always wrote one) and keeps it byte-identical; only nullability changes. Idempotent (DROP NOT NULL on an already-nullable column is a no-op success); unqualified names ride the runner's search_path; metadata-only DDL in its own transaction. A fail-loud postcondition asserts the column is nullable in the current schema, so a partial or skipped apply RAISEs and rolls back rather than letting the new pipeline's first batch-v2/synchronous run fail at insert. down() backfills NULL input_file_id with the empty-string sentinel '' (not a valid provider file id, aliases nothing) and restores SET NOT NULL — honest cost: the fact 'this run had no provider input file' is flattened to '', acceptable for a rollback to a pre-S6 image that only reads the column off rows its own OpenAI v1 pipeline wrote. SEQ 0090 — strictly greater than the max seq on live origin/main (core__0089_agent-assigned-skills); seq is assigned at MERGE, so a rename-only renumber of this module plus this fragment is normal if a concurrent change lands an intervening seq first (the runner tolerates gaps).
